topic: A synthesis should preserve disagreements in the evidence
grammarFocus: 学术论证的限定、因果、对比与证据范围
title: A synthesis should preserve disagreements in the evidence
instructions: 原创学术微训练；场景、机构与数值均为虚构模拟，不是事实报道或官方试题。先独立阅读答题，再用原句核对限定、比较与因果。短篇专项不能替代完整陌生测评。
passage:
A. In a fictional final-year project, a student reviewed three studies of extended library opening. One study reported more visits, another reported no change in exam results, and a third described improved access for evening workers. Her first summary called the evidence contradictory. Her supervisor suggested checking whether the studies were answering the same question before treating their conclusions as incompatible.

B. Visits, exam results and reported access were different outcomes. A library might attract more visits without changing examination performance. Workers could value later access even if they were not enrolled in examinations at all. Combining the results into a single average would require a defensible common measure, not merely three numbers. The student therefore built a comparison table listing each population, outcome and observation period.

C. Method also mattered. The visit count covered one branch over a holiday, whereas the exam study followed students through a full term. The access interviews recruited current evening users and omitted people unable to reach the branch. These limits did not make every finding worthless. They determined how widely each could reasonably be applied and which questions remained unanswered.

D. The student organised her synthesis around claims rather than around one paragraph per source. For each claim, she stated what the evidence supported, what qualified it and what further comparison would help. She kept a disagreement about staffing cost because the two reports used different definitions of overtime. Instead of choosing the more convenient figure, she explained why they could not yet be compared directly.

E. Her final recommendation was conditional: retain a limited evening service while collecting comparable information on cost and access. It was neither a guarantee of educational improvement nor an argument that uncertainty required permanent inaction. The review made a justified next step possible while preserving the boundary of the evidence. The supervisor asked her to keep the comparison table with the final paper so that readers could trace how each conclusion had been reached.
